question: On 28 January 2024, French Prime Minister Gabriel Attal said the following: ‘We will look at measures we can take regarding unfair competition. Our farmers are subject to rules that other (neighbouring) countries don't have to follow.’ These words, aimed at placating the French farmers’ protests against the French Government, are a serious attack on Spain’s agri-food sector.

As Gabriel Attal must surely know, the EU’s common market ensures equal conditions for all Member States. That is why the French Prime Minister’s statements – in addition to attacking our farmers and producers, who comply with EU regulations and quality standards – are unequivocally false and could cause serious problems in terms of the perception of reality. In view of this: 1.
Does the Commission condemn Gabriel Attal’s allegations of unfair competition directed towards Spain’s agri-food sector?
How will it protect Spanish producers from unfounded accusations by leaders of other Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.3.2024) 1. In general, the principles of the internal market in terms of mutual recognition of national technical rules, the removal of physical and technical barriers and standardisation, ensure a level playing field across Member States. For agriculture, this is ensured by the Common Organisation of the Market1, among others, with common marketing standards. 2.

The Commission has consistently recalled the importance of the free movement of goods as the cornerstone of the internal market. The Commission works to ensure the removal of obstacles to the free movement of goods.

Following a request from the Spanish authorities on 26 January 2024, it has requested the French authorities under Regulation 2679/98/EC2 to provide information about the recent incidents in French motorways and roads and about the measures they adopted or intended to adopt to facilitate the free movement of goods.

According to the French authorities, the disruptions started on 18 January 2024 but ended on 3 February 2024. There were isolated events provoking damages to goods but not to people, and the authorities provided real-time information about the traffic situation on the roads.
The Commission is in touch with the French authorities and will take the appropriate follow-up measures, taking into account any possible observations from other Member States.
1 Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 December 2013

establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products and repealing Council Regulations (EEC) No 922/72, (EEC) No 234/79, (EC) No 1037/2001 and (EC) No 1234/2007, OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, p. 671. 2 Council Regulation 2679/98/EC of 7 December 1998 on the functioning of the internal market in relation to the free movement of goods among the Member States, OJ L 337, 12.12.1998, p. 8–9.
